backlog.spec: Replace Morgan bits with all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors values (about 210 features). Replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the RandomForest (300 trees, max_features 0.3).
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF

backlog.spec: Concatenate the RDKit 2D descriptors (cleaned of NaN/inf) with Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits, count-based). Fit the RF on the combined matrix.
backlog.title: Descriptors + Morgan counts concatenated

backlog.spec: Use RDKit 2D descriptors with LGBMRegressor (n_estimators 500, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, verbose -1, random_state seed).
backlog.title: LightGBM on descriptors

backlog.spec: Use RDKit descriptors with CatBoostRegressor (iterations 800, depth 6, lr 0.05, loss MAE, thread_count 8, random_seed seed, verbose 0).
backlog.title: CatBoost on descriptors

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor on RDKit descriptors, with objective reg:absoluteerror, 600 trees, max_depth 4, lr 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, n_jobs 8.
backlog.title: XGBoost on descriptors with MAE objective

backlog.spec: Swap the RF for ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 2) on the RDKit descriptors.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees on descriptors

backlog.spec: Use a compact hand-picked feature set: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, aromatic ring count, charge-related counts, and LabuteASA. Fit a GradientBoostingRegressor with the huber loss. Permeability is mostly driven by polarity and size.
backlog.title: Small physchem feature set

backlog.spec: Average predictions from three models: an RF on descriptors, CatBoost on descriptors, and an RF on Morgan counts. Use equal weights.
backlog.title: Ensemble RF(desc)+CatBoost(desc)+RF(fp)

backlog.spec: Use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with radius 2 and 2048 bits in the original RF. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Morgan counts instead of bits

backlog.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (167 bits) with RDKit descriptors and fit an RF or ExtraTrees model.
backlog.title: MACCS keys + descriptors

backlog.spec: Add atom-pair count fingerprints (1024 bits) and the Morgan counts to the descriptor matrix. Fit LightGBM with strong column subsampling.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological torsion counts

backlog.spec: Use a Morgan generator with a feature-invariant atom generator (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen), radius 3, 1024 count bits. Concatenate it with the descriptors and fit an RF.
backlog.title: Feature-based Morgan (FCFP) plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Use a pipeline of QuantileTransformer or StandardScaler on cleaned descriptors, then SVR (C 3, epsilon 0.1, gamma scale). Descriptor-based kernels often beat trees on small data.
backlog.title: SVR with RBF on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (min/max form) with numpy. Fit SVR with kernel='precomputed' (C 5). Predict using the test×train kernel.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR / KRR

backlog.spec: Sum a Tanimoto kernel on the fingerprints and an RBF kernel on standardized descriptors. Fit KernelRidge with precomputed kernel, alpha 0.3.
backlog.title: GP-like kernel ridge on Tanimoto + descriptor RBF

backlog.spec: Switch the RF criterion to absolute_error, or use GradientBoostingRegressor(loss='absolute_error'). The metric is MAE, so predicting the conditional median may help.
backlog.title: Huber/MAE loss for trees

backlog.spec: On the descriptor RF, set min_samples_leaf=2, max_features=0.33 and n_estimators=500. Check whether less overfitting helps on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: RF min_samples_leaf and max_features tuning

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, build out-of-fold predictions with 5-fold inner CV for RF, LightGBM and SVR. Fit a Ridge meta-model with non-negative weights (positive=True) on them. Predict with base models refit on all data.
backlog.title: Inner-CV stacking

backlog.spec: Average 5 LightGBM models trained with different seeds (seed+i), using subsample 0.7, colsample 0.4, and extra_trees=True, on descriptors plus Morgan counts.
backlog.title: Multi-seed bagging of LightGBM

backlog.spec: Clip train_y to its 1st–99th percentile before fitting, to reduce the influence of outliers on the model. Predictions are not clipped.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing

backlog.spec: Add the EState VSA, SlogP_VSA, SMR_VSA and PEOE_VSA descriptor vectors (included in CalcMolDescriptors) and fragment-count features. Use a descriptor-only model with feature selection by RF importance (top 80 features) before the final fit.
backlog.title: Crippen/EState partial-charge features

backlog.spec: After computing the descriptors, drop columns with near-zero variance on the training set and columns with |corr| above 0.95. Fit the RF or LightGBM on what remains.
backlog.title: Remove low-variance and correlated features

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges (Uncharger). This gives clean features.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and canonicalization

backlog.spec: Add SMARTS-based counts of carboxylic acids, basic amines, amides, sulfonamides, phenols, quaternary N, and halogens. Append them to the descriptors for efficiency or P-gp-substrate signal. Fit LightGBM.
backlog.title: Add hydrogen-bond and polarity-specific counts

backlog.spec: Average CatBoost, LightGBM and XGBoost, all trained on descriptors plus Morgan counts at 512 bits. Use equal weights and modest depth 4–6.
backlog.title: Random-weighted mixed ensemble of GBMs

backlog.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden layers 256 and 64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping, adam) on QuantileTransformer-scaled descriptors. Average 5 seeds.
backlog.title: MLP on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Fit sklearn GaussianProcessRegressor on PCA-reduced (30 components), standardized descriptors. Use Matern kernel plus WhiteKernel, normalize_y=True.
backlog.title: Neural-free GP regression

backlog.spec: Embed each molecule with ETKDG (seed fixed) and compute rdMolDescriptors PMI1–3, NPR1/2, RadiusOfGyration and asphericity. Append them to the 2D descriptors for a LightGBM fit. Check the time budget.
backlog.title: Pseudo-3D shape descriptors

backlog.spec: With RF on descriptors, take the median of the individual tree predictions instead of the mean. It is more robust and fits the MAE metric.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees prediction

backlog.spec: Run CatBoost with depth 4, 1500 iterations, lr 0.03, l2_leaf_reg 5, rsm 0.3, using the descriptors plus 512-bit Morgan counts. Add early-stopping-free overfitting control via the l2 term.
backlog.title: Monotonic-free CatBoost with Morgan text features

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, featurize train and test once, then train 5 LGBMRegressor models with the same hyperparameters but seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 (vary subsample/colsample randomness) and return the mean of predictions. Keep the descriptor-only features. Aim is variance reduction.
backlog.title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging

backlog.spec: Change LGBMRegressor to objective='huber' with alpha=0.5 (or objective='l1' as an alternative if easy), keeping the other parameters. The target has outliers and the metric is MAE, so a robust loss may help.
backlog.title: Huber objective LightGBM

backlog.spec: Set num_leaves=7, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=5, colsample_bytree=0.3, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, and add extra_trees=True. Small data and scaffold-split shift favor shallower, more heavily regularized trees.
backlog.title: Stronger LightGBM regularization

backlog.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, as a numpy array) to the cleaned RDKit descriptor matrix in featurize, then train the same LightGBM.
backlog.title: Descriptors plus MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Compute hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) for train and test, reduce to 30 components with TruncatedSVD fitted on train only, and concatenate with the descriptors for LightGBM.
backlog.title: Descriptors plus atom-pair count SVD

backlog.spec: Replace the model with sklearn SVR (RBF, C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on descriptors after QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fitted on train, dropping zero-variance columns. Then average this prediction 50/50 with the current LightGBM prediction, as a bold different-inductive-bias blend.
backlog.title: SVR on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: After featurizing, fit on train only: drop columns with variance under 1e-8 and, among the remaining columns, drop one of each pair with absolute Pearson correlation above 0.95. Apply the same column mask to test, then train LightGBM.
backlog.title: Feature pruning by variance and correlation

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 1st and 99th percentiles (computed on train) to reduce the influence of extreme labels. Predictions are not clipped. Keep everything else the same.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing

backlog.spec: Build Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048) and compute a min/max Tanimoto kernel between molecules with numpy. Fit KernelRidge (precomputed kernel, alpha=0.5) on the train y minus its mean. Blend its predictions 30/70 with the descriptor LightGBM predictions. This combines the descriptor model with a substructure-similarity model.
backlog.title: Stacked LightGBM plus kernel ridge on Tanimoto

backlog.spec: In featurize, first keep only the largest fragment of each molecule (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser). Then append extra features: counts of H-bond donors and acceptors, TPSA/MolWt ratio, fraction of rotatable bonds, and the number of carboxylic acid, basic amine and amide groups via SMARTS matches. Train the same LightGBM.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and added polarity features

backlog.spec: Replace LightGBM with sklearn SVR (RBF kernel, C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on RDKit descriptors. Preprocess inside fit_predict: fit QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=200) on train features only, drop zero-variance columns, then fit SVR and predict test. Keep featurize unchanged.
backlog.title: SVR on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the model with SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Compute 2048-bit Morgan radius-2 count fingerprints, then use the MinMax (generalized Tanimoto) kernel K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) computed with numpy in chunks for train-train and test-train. Predict with the precomputed test kernel. No descriptors.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Average predictions of the current descriptor LightGBM (0.6 weight) and an SVR with a precomputed MinMax Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits, C=5, 0.4 weight). Different feature views should give diverse errors. Implement the kernel with numpy chunks.
backlog.title: Stack LightGBM with Tanimoto SVR

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, featurize train and test once, then train 8 LightGBM models with seeds seed..seed+7 (subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.4) and return the mean of their predictions. Otherwise keep the current hyperparameters.
backlog.title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging

backlog.spec: Change LightGBM params to num_leaves=7, min_child_samples=20, colsample_bytree=0.3, reg_lambda=5, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, and add extra_trees=True. This targets overfitting on 728 molecules with unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Stronger LightGBM regularization

backlog.spec: Append to the RDKit descriptors the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) and 512-bit feature-Morgan (useFeatures via rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2) count fingerprints. Keep the LightGBM model. Slot 9 hinted that extra fingerprint views help slightly.
backlog.title: Descriptors plus MACCS keys and FCFP counts

backlog.spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep the largest fragment via rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(asMols=True) choosing max heavy atoms, then compute descriptors on it. Also add the number of fragments as a feature. Keep LightGBM unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest-fragment canonicalization

backlog.spec: Replace LightGBM with an average of 5 sklearn MLPRegressor models (hidden layers (256,64), alpha=1e-1, early_stopping=True, max_iter=500, seeds seed+i). Inputs are descriptors transformed with QuantileTransformer(normal) fit on train, zero-variance columns dropped. Return the mean of the 5 predictions.
backlog.title: MLP ensemble on quantile-scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Clip train_y to the 2nd and 98th percentiles of train_y before fitting LightGBM, and set objective='huber' with alpha=0.4. Predictions are not clipped except to the same bounds. This reduces the influence of extreme permeability outliers on MAE.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing with L1-leaning loss

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the SVR from C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale' to C=5, epsilon=0.05, keeping gamma='scale'. Everything else stays the same. This probes whether a less regularized SVR improves the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C/epsilon/gamma

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM 5 times with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 (each with subsample 0.8 and colsample 0.5 as now) and average their predictions to form p_lgb. Reuse the already computed feature matrices. Keep the SVR blend 50/50.
backlog.title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM parameters to num_leaves=7, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=5, colsample_bytree=0.3, n_estimators=700, learning_rate=0.03. Leave the SVR and the 50/50 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Stronger LightGBM regularization

backlog.spec: Add sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden_layer_sizes=(128,64), alpha=1e-1, early_stopping=False, max_iter=300, adam) fitted on the quantile-normalized descriptors Str. Average 5 seeds (seed..seed+4). Final prediction = (p_lgb + p_svr + p_mlp)/3.
backlog.title: MLP member on quantile-normalized descriptors

backlog.spec: Before fitting both models, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles computed on the training fold. Predict as before, and do not clip the test predictions.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing

backlog.spec: In featurize, parse each molecule, keep only the largest fragment with rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(asMols=True) (choose max by GetNumHeavyAtoms), then compute the descriptors on it. Fall back to the original molecule if that fails.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: After the keep (std>0) mask, drop descriptors for the SVR input only: compute the absolute correlation matrix on Str and greedily drop any column with |r|>0.95 against an already kept column. Fit the SVR on the reduced set. LightGBM keeps all features.
backlog.title: Prune correlated descriptors for SVR

backlog.spec: Compute 167-bit MACCS keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule. Concatenate them to the quantile-normalized descriptors for the SVR only, scaled by 0.5 so they do not dominate the RBF kernel. Also append them to the LightGBM features.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys to the SVR input

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold KFold (seeded) on the training set. Get out-of-fold predictions from LightGBM and the SVR, then fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True, with intercept) on the two columns. Refit both models on the full training set and combine them with the learned weights instead of 0.5/0.5. This adds roughly 6 times the compute.
backlog.title: Stacked blend weights via inner CV

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member: KNeighborsRegressor (k=7, weights='distance', metric='cosine') on the quantile-normalized descriptors Str. Final prediction = 0.4*p_lgb + 0.4*p_svr + 0.2*p_knn.
backlog.title: Bolder: SVR on rank-averaged diverse kernels plus kNN

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the SVR hyperparameters from C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale' to C=5, epsilon=0.05 and gamma=0.5/n_features_kept (about half of 'scale' given quantile-normal unit-variance inputs). Keep everything else identical, including the 50/50 blend with LightGBM.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C/epsilon/gamma

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, in featurize() parse each SMILES, keep only the largest fragment using rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(asMols=True) and choose the one with the most heavy atoms, then compute the descriptors on it. Fall back to the original molecule if parsing the fragments fails. No other change.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: At the start of fit_predict, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles (computed on the training fold only) before fitting both LightGBM and SVR. Predictions are not clipped. This limits the influence of extreme permeability values on the models.
backlog.title: Winsorize training target

backlog.spec: Change the final return to 0.4*p_lgb + 0.6*svr.predict(Ste). The SVR is a diverse and strong member, so shifting weight to it may help. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.4/0.6 toward SVR

backlog.spec: For the SVR branch only, after the keep-variance mask, drop descriptors whose absolute Pearson correlation with an earlier kept column exceeds 0.95 (computed on training features after quantile transform). Fit the SVR on the reduced matrix. LightGBM keeps all features.
backlog.title: Prune correlated descriptors for SVR

backlog.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (k=7, weights='distance', Euclidean) on the same quantile-normalized matrix used by the SVR. Final prediction is 0.4*LightGBM + 0.4*SVR + 0.2*kNN. This is a bolder, local-similarity member that is structurally diverse.
backlog.title: Add kNN regressor on quantile-normal descriptors as third member

backlog.spec: Add a second SVR with a precomputed min/max Tanimoto kernel on 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2), C=3, epsilon=0.1. Combine the three predictions (LightGBM, descriptor SVR, Tanimoto SVR) by taking their median per molecule rather than the mean. The median reduces the influence of a member that is off.
backlog.title: Median-style robust blend with a second SVR on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the SVR to C=10, epsilon=0.05, gamma='scale' multiplied by 0.5 (i.e. gamma=0.5/(n_features*Str.var())). Keep everything else identical. Goal is a smoother, higher-capacity RBF member in the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C/epsilon/gamma

backlog.spec: At the start of fit_predict, clip y to the 2nd and 98th percentiles of the training y (np.percentile) before fitting both LightGBM and SVR. Predictions are not clipped. Reduces the influence of outlier labels on MAE.
backlog.title: Winsorize training target

backlog.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor(n_neighbors=7, weights='distance') on the quantile-normalized descriptor matrix Str/Ste (already computed for the SVR). Blend as 0.4*LGB + 0.4*SVR + 0.2*kNN.
backlog.title: kNN third blend member

backlog.spec: For the SVR input only, after the QuantileTransformer, drop columns whose absolute Pearson correlation with an earlier kept column exceeds 0.95 (computed on training Str; apply the same mask to Ste). LightGBM input stays unchanged. Lowers redundant-feature dominance in the RBF distance.
backlog.title: Prune correlated descriptors for SVR

backlog.spec: Add an RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1) on 1024-bit radius-2 Morgan count fingerprints, transformed with log1p and then standardized. Blend as 0.4*LGB + 0.4*descriptor SVR + 0.2*FP SVR. Differs from the earlier Tanimoto kernel attempt in using a plain RBF on log-scaled counts.
backlog.title: Second SVR on Morgan count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM prediction with a bagged ensemble of 7 LightGBM models, each trained on a different 80% row subsample and seed. Take the median of their predictions instead of the mean. Then blend 50/50 with the SVR as before.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees LightGBM readout

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with 8 SVRs, each fit on a random 60% of the quantile-normalized descriptor columns (rng seeded from seed). Average their predictions, then blend 50/50 with LightGBM. Adds feature-level diversity to the kernel member.
backlog.title: Feature-subset diverse SVR bagging

backlog.spec: Fit the SVR on y standardized to zero mean and unit variance, with C=1.5, then invert the transform on its predictions. This makes epsilon and C scale-free relative to y. Keep LightGBM on the raw y.
backlog.title: Target transform via rank-normal quantiles for SVR

backlog.spec: Compute 5-fold out-of-fold SVR predictions on the training set (using seed-controlled KFold). Append them as an extra feature column to the descriptors for LightGBM. For test, use the SVR fit on all training data. Final prediction is 0.5*LGB(with the SVR feature) + 0.5*SVR. This tries to let the trees correct the kernel model's errors.
backlog.title: Bolder: Stack with ridge on out-of-fold SVR residual features

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, build extra features: 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) and 512-bit feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, useFeatures via rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen). Concatenate them to the RDKit descriptors for the LightGBM member only; the SVR keeps seeing just the quantile-normalized descriptors. Keep the 50/50 blend. Run it once; the earlier combined version gave 0.3599/0.3615.
backlog.title: MACCS+FCFP counts for LightGBM only

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member: an RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on 2048-bit radius-2 Morgan count fingerprints transformed with log1p. Final prediction = 0.4*LightGBM + 0.4*descriptor SVR + 0.2*fingerprint SVR.
backlog.title: Second SVR on Morgan counts, three-way blend

backlog.spec: For the SVR member only, fit on y transformed to the normal scores of its ranks (scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n)), then map the SVR predictions back with np.interp on the sorted training y against the sorted normal scores. LightGBM keeps the raw y. Blend 50/50 as before.
backlog.title: Rank-normal target transform for SVR

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with an average of 8 SVRs, each trained on a random 60% subset of the quantile-normalized descriptor columns (rng seeded by seed). Use the same hyperparameters (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'). Keep the 50/50 blend with LightGBM.
backlog.title: SVR feature-subset bagging

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM first. Get out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set with 5-fold KFold, and compute the residuals. Fit the SVR (C=1, epsilon=0.1) on the quantile-normalized descriptors to predict those residuals. The final prediction = LightGBM prediction + 0.7*SVR residual prediction. This replaces the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Residual stacking: SVR on LightGBM residuals

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM member to boosting_type='dart' (n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.05, drop_rate=0.1, num_leaves=15, colsample_bytree=0.5, subsample 0.8). Keep the SVR and the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Descriptor-wise LightGBM with DART

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM on all descriptors, keep the top 80 features by gain importance, and then refit LightGBM and the SVR on only those columns (the quantile transformer too). Keep the 50/50 blend. This trades noise features for a smaller, cleaner input.
backlog.title: Inner-CV feature selection by LightGBM importance

backlog.spec: Train the SVR on the training set concatenated with 2 noisy copies of the quantile-normalized descriptors (Gaussian noise sd 0.15, rng seeded by seed) with the same targets. LightGBM is unchanged. Keep the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Add Gaussian-noise augmentation for SVR

backlog.spec: Compute 5-fold out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training set (using the seed). Fit the RBF SVR (C=3, eps=0.1) on the quantile-normalized descriptors to predict the residual y minus the OOF prediction. Final prediction = full LightGBM prediction + 0.7 * SVR residual prediction. This replaces the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Residual SVR on LightGBM out-of-fold residuals

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with an average of 10 RBF SVRs (C=3, eps=0.1, gamma='scale'). Each is fit on a random 60% column subset of the quantile-normalized descriptors, drawn with np.random.RandomState(seed+i). Average their predictions and blend 50/50 with LightGBM.
backlog.title: SVR feature-subset bagging

backlog.spec: For the SVR only, stack the quantile-normalized training matrix Str with 2 noisy copies (Gaussian noise sd 0.1, drawn from RandomState(seed)). Repeat the targets to match, and fit the SVR on the stacked set. Keep the 50/50 blend with LightGBM.
backlog.title: Gaussian-noise augmentation for SVR

backlog.spec: Build three predictions: LightGBM, the descriptor SVR, and a second RBF SVR on sqrt-transformed 1024-bit Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, gamma='scale', C=3). Return the median of the three per molecule, instead of the mean.
backlog.title: Median blend with Morgan-count SVR

backlog.spec: Keep the quantile-normal descriptors. Compute PCA with 40 components (whiten=True, random_state=seed) on the training set. Append those components to the raw descriptors as extra LightGBM features. Fit the SVR on the PCA components only, with gamma='scale'. Blend 50/50.
backlog.title: Descriptor-space PCA-whitened SVR plus LightGBM on PCA components

backlog.spec: Keep the current 50/50 LightGBM/SVR blend. Append 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, as float32) plus 512-bit feature-Morgan (useFeatures=True, radius 2) count fingerprints to the descriptor matrix used only by LightGBM. The SVR keeps descriptors only, with its quantile transform fitted on descriptor columns only. Past runs of MACCS+FCFP gave 0.3599/0.3615.
backlog.title: MACCS for LightGBM only, retry with replicate

backlog.spec: Before featurizing in featurize(), parse each SMILES and keep only the largest fragment by heavy atom count (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True, choose max by GetNumHeavyAtoms). Neutralize charges with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Fall back to the original mol on any exception. Everything else stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: For the SVR member only, transform y to normal scores with a QuantileTransformer (output_distribution='normal') fitted on train_y. Fit the SVR on those scores, then invert the predictions with inverse_transform, clipped to the train y range. LightGBM keeps the raw y. The blend is unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-normal target transform for SVR

backlog.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (k=7, weights='distance', Euclidean) on the quantile-normalized descriptors, after selecting the 60 descriptors with the highest LightGBM gain importance. Blend weights: 0.4 LightGBM, 0.4 SVR, 0.2 kNN.
backlog.title: kNN third blend member

backlog.spec: For the SVR only, augment the quantile-normalized training matrix with 2 extra copies. Each copy has N(0, 0.1) noise added to every feature and the same y. Fit the SVR on the stacked 3n rows with C=3. LightGBM is unchanged. Blend 50/50.
backlog.title: Gaussian-noise augmentation for SVR

backlog.spec: Switch the LightGBM member to boosting_type='dart' with 400 trees, drop_rate 0.1, learning_rate 0.06, and other params unchanged. Keep the SVR blend. If dart is too slow, use linear_tree=True with linear_lambda=1.0 instead.
backlog.title: LightGBM DART with linear trees

backlog.spec: Change the blend to 0.35*LightGBM + 0.65*SVR. Clip the final predictions to [min(train_y)-0.2, max(train_y)+0.2]. This is a one-line change and tests whether the SVR deserves more weight.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.35/0.65 toward SVR plus clipping

backlog.spec: Build a precomputed kernel K = 0.6*RBF(quantile-normalized descriptors, gamma=1/(n_features*var)) + 0.4*MinMax-Tanimoto(Morgan counts, radius 2, 2048 bits). Compute the MinMax kernel with a vectorized numpy loop over test rows, not an n×n×d tensor. Fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=3, epsilon=0.1) on K. Use it in place of the RBF SVR in the 50/50 blend with LightGBM.
backlog.title: Bolder: multi-kernel SVR on concatenated descriptor RBF and Morgan Tanimoto kernels

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest fragment by heavy atom count (rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols=True, then max by GetNumHeavyAtoms), and neutralize charges with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Fall back to the original molecule if anything fails. Featurize the cleaned molecules for both LightGBM and SVR. Everything else stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor (k=7, distance weights, cosine or euclidean metric) fit on the quantile-normalized descriptors (the same Str/Ste used by the SVR). Final prediction = 0.4*LightGBM + 0.4*SVR + 0.2*kNN.
backlog.title: kNN third blend member

backlog.spec: Add a second SVR (RBF, C=3) on the quantile-normalized descriptors concatenated with MACCS keys scaled by 0.3, as a third member. Final prediction = (LightGBM + descriptor SVR + MACCS SVR)/3.
backlog.title: Bolder: SVR bagging over MACCS-augmented rank features

backlog.spec: Change the final blend to 0.35*p_lgb + 0.65*svr prediction, nothing else. Clipping the output to the training y min/max range is also fine.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.35 LightGBM / 0.65 SVR

backlog.spec: Set linear_tree=True in LGBMRegressor, with linear_lambda=1.0, num_leaves=7 and n_estimators=300. Feed it the quantile-normalized descriptors (the same transform as for the SVR) instead of the raw ones, so linear leaves are well conditioned. Keep the SVR blend.
backlog.title: Extra-trees-mode LightGBM with linear leaves

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run inner 5-fold CV on the train set (KFold, shuffle, seeded) to get out-of-fold predictions from LightGBM, the descriptor SVR, kNN (k=7) and ExtraTrees (300 trees, max_features 0.5). Fit a non-negative Ridge on these 4 columns, with intercept. Refit all the bases on the full train set and combine their test predictions with the learned weights.
backlog.title: Bolder: out-of-fold stacked ridge on diverse bases

backlog.spec: Add a helper clean(smiles) that parses each SMILES with Chem.MolFromSmiles, keeps the largest fragment via rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser().choose(m) (from rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize import rdMolStandardize), and returns the mol. Use the cleaned mol in featurize and extra_feats for both train and test. Fall back to the original mol if cleaning raises an exception. Leave the models unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: Set linear_tree=True and linear_lambda=1.0 in the LGBMRegressor, with num_leaves=7 and min_child_samples=30. Keep the features and the SVR unchanged. To keep linear leaves stable, pass the LightGBM a feature matrix where the descriptor columns are clipped to the 1st/99th percentiles of the training data.
backlog.title: LightGBM with linear_tree

backlog.spec: Set boosting_type='dart', drop_rate=0.1, n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.05 in LGBMRegressor and leave the rest unchanged. Dropout of trees gives a different regularization than shrinkage.
backlog.title: LightGBM DART mode

backlog.spec: Build OOF predictions (5-fold KFold, seed) on the training set for LightGBM, the descriptor SVR, and an ExtraTrees (300 trees, max_features 0.5) on the descriptors. Fit a non-negative Ridge (positive=True, alpha=1) on those OOF predictions plus intercept, then refit the bases on all data and combine the test predictions with it. Keep n_jobs=8 and watch the runtime.
backlog.title: Ridge-stacked diverse bases

backlog.spec: Compute each training molecule's mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training neighbours using Morgan bit fingerprints. Weight samples by 1/(0.5+sim) so that isolated scaffolds count more, and pass the weights to LGBMRegressor.fit and SVR.fit (sample_weight). Normalize the weights to mean 1.
backlog.title: Sample weights by density

backlog.spec: Add path_smooth=5, reg_alpha=0.5, and min_split_gain=0.0 to LightGBM, with feature_fraction_bynode=0.5 and colsample_bytree=0.7. Keep everything else unchanged. This tests node-level feature subsampling on the wider feature set.
backlog.title: Monotone-free feature bagging per tree with extra regularization via path smoothing

backlog.spec: For the SVR input only, append the 167 MACCS keys to the descriptor matrix before the QuantileTransformer. Down-weight them by multiplying the MACCS block by 0.5 after the transform, so descriptors dominate the RBF kernel. LightGBM is unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair SVD plus MACCS for SVR

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with the mean of three SVRs on the same quantile-normalized descriptors, using gamma = 0.5/d, 1/d and 2/d (d = number of kept features), C=3 each and epsilon=0.1. Blend 50/50 with LightGBM as before.
backlog.title: Rank-average of SVR across several gammas

backlog.spec: Self-training: fit the current blend on the training set, predict the test molecules, then refit LightGBM and the SVR on train plus test with the pseudo-labels, using sample weight 0.3 for the test rows. Return the refit blend's predictions for the test molecules. This uses unlabelled test structures, which fit_predict already receives.
backlog.title: Auxiliary targets via pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Add a helper that parses each SMILES, keeps only the largest fragment by heavy-atom count using rdkit.Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags(asMols=True), and neutralizes charges with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Use this cleaned mol in featurize and extra_feats for both train and test. If parsing fails, fall back to the original mol. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and largest fragment

backlog.spec: In the LightGBM model, set boosting_type='dart', drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, n_estimators=600 and learning_rate=0.05. Keep the other parameters and the 50/50 SVR blend. DART is a different regularizer and may generalize better on 728 molecules.
backlog.title: LightGBM DART mode

backlog.spec: Compute each training molecule's mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training neighbours using the 512-bit Morgan bit vectors. Weight each sample by 1/(0.5+meansim), and normalize the weights to mean 1. This down-weights dense chemical series. Pass the weights as sample_weight to LGBMRegressor.fit and SVR.fit.
backlog.title: Density-based sample weights

backlog.spec: Train 6 LightGBM models. Each uses a different random 80% of the Murcko scaffold groups of the training set, assigned via the seed. Average their predictions as the LightGBM member of the blend. This diversifies the models in a scaffold-aware way, unlike plain seed bagging.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bagging of LightGBM

backlog.spec: Fit the current blend on the training data. Predict the test molecules, which are unlabeled, and add them to the training set with weight 0.3, using the blend predictions as labels. Refit both LightGBM and the SVR on this augmented set and return the new blend predictions. Pass sample_weight to both models. This is transductive and uses the test SMILES only.
backlog.title: Auxiliary pseudo-label self-training

backlog.spec: Replace the single LightGBM with an average of 4 LightGBM models. Each is trained on the features plus Gaussian noise (sd 0.05 times each column's std) added to the continuous descriptor columns. Use a different noise draw per model, seeded from seed. Keep the SVR and the 50/50 blend. The aim is smoother trees.
backlog.title: Dropout-style noisy descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member: sklearn KernelRidge with kernel='laplacian', alpha=0.5, gamma=1/(4*n_features), fit on the quantile-normalized descriptors. Use blend weights of 0.4 LightGBM, 0.4 SVR and 0.2 KernelRidge. The L1-distance kernel is more robust than RBF on heavy-tailed descriptors.
backlog.title: Kernel-ridge on quantile descriptors with Laplacian kernel

backlog.spec: Append a few ratio features to the descriptors for both models. They are TPSA/MolWt, MolLogP minus 0.01*TPSA, HBD/(HBA+1), NumRotatableBonds/HeavyAtomCount, and FractionCSP3*MolLogP. Compute them from the existing descriptor columns by name via Descriptors.descList indices. Permeability depends on polarity and size balance, so trees can use these directly.
backlog.title: Custom physchem interaction features

backlog.spec: Use the SVR as a base learner. Compute 5-fold out-of-fold SVR predictions on the training set. Fit LightGBM with init_score set to the OOF SVR predictions, so it boosts the correction. At test time, add the full-fit SVR prediction to the LightGBM output. Use a low learning rate of 0.02 with 300 trees. The final prediction is 0.5*SVR + 0.5*(SVR + LGB correction), with a shrink factor of 0.7 on the correction. This is boosting from a kernel baseline, not residual stacking via an SVR.
backlog.title: Two-stage LightGBM with SVR prediction offset

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, set the LightGBM member to boosting_type='dart' with n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, keeping num_leaves=15, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10. Keep the MACCS+FCFP features and the 50/50 blend with the descriptor SVR unchanged.
backlog.title: LightGBM DART mode

backlog.spec: Replace the RBF SVR with an SVR using a precomputed Laplacian kernel exp(-gamma*L1 distance) on the quantile-normalized descriptors (sklearn.metrics.pairwise.laplacian_kernel, gamma=1/(n_features*2)), C=3, epsilon=0.1. Keep the 50/50 blend with LightGBM.
backlog.title: Laplacian-kernel SVR member

backlog.spec: Compute each training molecule's mean Euclidean distance to its 5 nearest neighbours in the quantile-normalized descriptor space. Use weights proportional to 1/(1+z), with z the standardized distance, clipped to [0.5,1.5]. Pass them as sample_weight to both LightGBM and SVR. Test molecules from unseen scaffolds are often sparse, so this may change which regions the models fit best.
backlog.title: Density-based sample weights

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with 900 trees and a learning-rate schedule from 0.06 decaying to 0.01 using lightgbm.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda i: 0.01+0.05*0.5*(1+cos(pi*i/900))). Keep other settings and the blend as they are.
backlog.title: Cosine LR decay via callbacks

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out about 15% of the training scaffold groups (grouped by Murcko scaffold, seeded) as a validation set. Fit LightGBM with 1500 trees and early stopping (50 rounds) using L1 metric. Then refit on all training data with the best iteration count, scaled by 1.1. Blend as before.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware early stopping of LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models. For each, multiply the training feature matrix by a random Bernoulli mask (keep prob 0.9) applied to descriptor columns only, setting dropped entries to NaN so LightGBM treats them as missing. Average the models' predictions on the clean test features, then blend 50/50 with the SVR.
backlog.title: Feature-noise dropout LightGBM bagging

backlog.spec: Compute 5-fold out-of-fold SVR predictions on the training set. Fit LightGBM with init_score set to those OOF SVR predictions, so it learns y minus SVR. At test time, use SVR(full fit) prediction plus the LightGBM output, shrunk by 0.8. Return that value as the final prediction and drop the 50/50 blend.
backlog.title: Two-stage LightGBM on SVR offset

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member, KernelRidge (alpha=0.5, kernel='laplacian', gamma=1/(2*n_features)) on the quantile-normalized descriptors. Use weights 0.4 LightGBM, 0.4 SVR and 0.2 KRR.
backlog.title: Heteroscedastic-noise-free GP on SVR-ish kernel ensemble: Kernel ridge with Laplacian kernel

backlog.spec: After the first blend prediction, treat the test molecules as unlabeled. Add them to the training set with the blend predictions as pseudo-labels and weight 0.3. Refit both LightGBM and SVR (SVR via sample_weight) and return the 50/50 blend of the refit models. Test SMILES are available in fit_predict.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training

backlog.spec: Append to the LightGBM feature matrix, which already has descriptors, MACCS and FCFP counts, 20 TruncatedSVD components of 2048-bit atom-pair count fingerprints. Fit the SVD on train and test SMILES together (unsupervised). Leave the SVR input unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair SVD plus MACCS for LightGBM

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute for each training molecule the mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest other training molecules on 2048-bit Morgan bit fingerprints (via numpy dot products). Set weight = 1/(0.5+meansim), normalized to mean 1, so molecules in dense clusters are downweighted. Pass as sample_weight to LGBMRegressor.fit and SVR.fit. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Density-based sample weights

backlog.spec: After fitting the 50/50 blend, predict the test molecules, then refit the SVR on train plus test molecules using the blend predictions as pseudo-labels with sample_weight 0.3 (train weight 1). Use the refit SVR in the final 50/50 blend with LightGBM, which stays trained on train only. The quantile transformer is fit on train plus test descriptors (unsupervised).
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training on test molecules

backlog.spec: Fit the QuantileTransformer for the SVR on the descriptors of train and test molecules stacked together (unsupervised, no labels). Keep the SVR hyperparameters and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive quantile transform

backlog.spec: Train a second LightGBM on the quantile-normal rank transform of y (scipy rankdata mapped through norm.ppf), then map its predictions back by interpolating onto the sorted train_y. Average this with the regular LightGBM before the 50/50 SVR blend, i.e. LightGBM part = mean of the two.
backlog.title: Multi-output auxiliary target: LightGBM on SVR-rank target

backlog.spec: Add path_smooth=10, min_split_gain=0.0, reg_alpha=0.5 and max_bin=63 to the LightGBM params, and set feature_fraction_bynode=0.5 with colsample_bytree 0.7. Leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Path smoothing and extra regularization in LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with the mean of 15 RBF SVRs (same C, epsilon, gamma), each fit on a bootstrap sample of 85% of the training rows drawn without replacement using rng seeded by seed. Quantile transform is fit once on all train rows.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR over bootstrap samples

backlog.spec: Fit sklearn Ridge (alpha tuned by RidgeCV over [1,10,100,1000]) on log1p 1024-bit Morgan count fingerprints concatenated with the quantile-normalized descriptors. Combine as 0.4 LightGBM, 0.5 SVR, 0.1 Ridge. Everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Add a small 1D-CNN-free ridge on Morgan counts as an error-diverse third member

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute each training molecule's mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest other training molecules using 2048-bit Morgan bit fingerprints (RDKit BulkTanimotoSimilarity). Set the LightGBM sample_weight to 1/(0.5+mean_sim), then normalize the weights to mean 1. This down-weights dense clusters of analogs and up-weights rare scaffolds. Leave the SVR and the 50/50 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Density-based sample weights for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Fit the QuantileTransformer on the descriptor rows of train and test molecules stacked together (no labels used). Then transform both sets and fit the SVR on the transformed train rows. Compute the variance filter `keep` on the stacked matrix too. Leave LightGBM and the 50/50 blend unchanged. This tests whether seeing the test descriptor distribution helps the SVR on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Transductive quantile transform for SVR

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with the mean of 15 RBF SVRs (C=3, eps=0.1, gamma='scale'). Fit each on a bootstrap sample of the training rows drawn with rng=np.random.RandomState(seed+i), using the shared quantile-normalized features. Keep LightGBM and the 50/50 blend. This reduces SVR variance through row resampling, which differs from the column-subset bagging already tried.
backlog.title: Bootstrap-bagged SVR

backlog.spec: Make the first blend prediction p on the test set. Then refit the LightGBM with the test molecules added as extra rows, with targets p and sample weight 0.3. Use the refit LightGBM prediction in the 50/50 blend with the SVR (the SVR stays trained on the real labels only). This is transductive self-training for unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training on test molecules

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM parameters to path_smooth=10, min_child_samples=15, feature_fraction_bynode=0.5, colsample_bytree=0.7, and n_estimators=700 at lr 0.03. Keep the slot-52 features. This is a regularization change aimed at the leaf values rather than the tree structure.
backlog.title: LightGBM path smoothing with extra-trees and larger min_data

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with 600 estimators using the callback lightgbm.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda i: 0.002 + 0.5*(0.05-0.002)*(1+np.cos(np.pi*i/600))). Keep the other parameters and the slot-52 features. A schedule that starts at 0.05 and decays to 0.002 may fit the fine detail better than the constant lr of 0.03.
backlog.title: Cosine-decayed learning rate for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Keep the predictions of LightGBM and the SVR. Map each to its rank within the test set and average the ranks with equal weights. Then map the averaged rank back to values through the quantiles of the training y (np.quantile(y, rank/(n-1))). If the test set has fewer than 20 molecules, fall back to the plain average. This tests whether the blend is better done in rank space.
backlog.title: Rank-average blend instead of value average

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, pick the SVR C from {1,3,10} and gamma multiplier from {0.5,1,2} by 4-fold GroupKFold on the training set. Group by Murcko scaffold, using MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles. Score by MAE on the quantile-normalized features. Refit with the best pair and keep the 50/50 blend. This tunes the SVR by scaffold-split validation inside each fold, which differs from the fixed retunings already tried.
backlog.title: Two-view SVR from scaffold-aware GroupKFold hyperparameter choice

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member, sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor (loss='absolute_error', max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=400, l2_regularization=1.0, random_state=seed). Train it on the slot-52 LightGBM feature set. Use weights 0.3 LightGBM, 0.4 SVR, 0.3 HGB. This brings in a different tree learner trained directly on the MAE metric.
backlog.title: Monotone-smoothed target: add MAE-trained 2-layer ensemble via sklearn HistGradientBoosting

backlog.spec: After the quantile normalization, multiply the columns of the descriptor matrix by importance weights before the SVR. Obtain the weights from a quick LightGBM fit on the training data. Use w_j = sqrt(gain_j / mean_gain) clipped to [0.3, 3], where gain_j is the feature's gain importance. This gives an ARD-like RBF kernel. Keep the blend and the LightGBM unchanged. The LightGBM must be fit only on the training fold.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-count-weighted kernel SVR with descriptor group scaling

incumbent.description: Append MACCS keys and 512-bit feature-Morgan counts to the descriptor matrix for LightGBM only, with the SVR kept on descriptors only.

memo:
Helped: richer features and boosting. Descriptors plus Morgan counts cut loss from 0.4417 to 0.3917. LightGBM gave 0.3722. A 50/50 blend with an RBF SVR on quantile-normalized descriptors gave 0.3650/0.3656. The incumbent (slot 52, 0.3574 over 2 runs) gives LightGBM MACCS keys plus 512-bit feature-Morgan counts, with the SVR on descriptors only.
Did not help: model swaps (CatBoost 0.3894, RF 0.3903, XGBoost 0.3808, ExtraTrees 0.3768), pure SVR (0.3849), Tanimoto kernels (0.3764, 0.4176), GP (0.3690), MLP (0.3687), kNN (0.3636), stacking (0.3621, 0.3584), SVR retuning, blend reweighting (0.3643), feature selection (0.3718), PCA (0.3752), DART (0.3744). Seed bagging, Huber, target clipping, physchem/salt features, early stopping (0.3608) and a ridge member (0.3603) were within noise (sd about 0.0037) or worse.
Next: ideas are nearly exhausted. Try small LightGBM tuning on the slot 52 feature set, or atom-pair SVD (0.3648 alone). Avoid the lists above and aborted repeats. Consider stopping.
